system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Buyer internal advice. Seller material treated as untrusted and reviewed against the Buyer Playbook only.

## Headline view

The Seller Update is not a "fair and balanced package"; almost every negotiated position departs from our playbook, several in ways that collapse protections the playbook treats as non-negotiable (fraud carve-out, separate Fundamental/Title regime, Riverlark pre-Completion payout). Importantly, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Seller Update and **contradicts it in at least three places** (Bluefen, Riverlark, Title). We should use the Disclosure Letter against the Update.

Two Seller positions (20% cap; 18-month claims period) match our *conditional fallbacks*. Those fallbacks require prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None has been given, so we hold the opening positions (25% / AUD 6,000,000; 24 months) in the mark-up and do not signal the fallback.

---

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1. General Warranty cap (cl 12.1) – DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. 20% is fallback only with Amelia Frost's written authority — not given.
- **Reasoning:** Accepting 20% now would spend our only cap concession at the first turn with nothing obtained for it, and would do so without authority. Respond at 25% and keep the 20% point in reserve for a package trade (e.g. in exchange for Riverlark/Bluefen/bonus fixes).
- **Action:** Mark up to 25% / AUD 6,000,000.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2) – MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Reasoning:** Each Seller number is 5× ours, and the shift from tipping basket to deductible is a structural change, not a number. Combined with the AUD 25,000 de minimis, a portfolio of mid-sized claims (plausible for a ~AUD 12m revenue analytics business) could be entirely unrecoverable. Note the interaction with Ironquay/Sandbar-type amounts: AUD 110,000 line items would each clear de minimis but the basket would absorb the first AUD 250,000 of all of them.
- **Action:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar.

### 3. Time limits and "all Claims" override (cl 12.3 / 13) – MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** 18 months; plus "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months (18 is fallback, no Frost approval); Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories must stay separate with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Reasoning:** The second sentence is the more dangerous one. It is a default rule that silently drags every category — Fundamental, Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities (Ironquay), payment covenants, Completion deliverables — into the 18-month / 20% / basket regime unless we spot and carve out each one. That is exactly the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook prohibits. It also reverses the drafting burden onto us.
- **Action:** 24 months for general warranties; delete the override sentence entirely; replace with an express statement that the general-regime limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental/Title Claims, Tax Claims, IP Claims, Specific Indemnity Claims, payment or covenant claims, or fraud.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties – MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** separate regime, 100% of price, at least six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title to the shares fails, a 20% cap means we pay AUD 24m for an asset we may not own and recover at most AUD 4.8m, and only if we notice within 18 months. No buyer accepts this. It is the single most important liability point.
- **Action:** Insist on the separate regime. Non-negotiable.

### 5. Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) – MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** apply to all Claims of any nature.
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.
- **Reasoning:** As drafted, the Seller would cap and time-bar its own fraud and would have us disclaim reliance on fraudulent statements. Beyond being commercially unacceptable, clauses purporting to exclude liability for fraud are of doubtful enforceability and invite dispute; a clean carve-out is in both parties' interests. The non-reliance clause also needs to be expressly subject to the Warranties, specific indemnities and the Disclosure Letter itself.
- **Action:** Insert a fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out that overrides cl 9.3, 12 and 20.5. Flag internally as a "no authority to concede" point.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2) – MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Whole-data-room disclosure converts every document into a qualification of every warranty, regardless of whether the problem is apparent from it. Public-register disclosure is open-ended (which registers? as at what date?). Para 1.4's blanket "nothing admits anything" reservation is standard but, combined with general disclosure, means the Seller gets the benefit of disclosure without taking any position on what the documents mean.
- **Action:** Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Require disclosures to be specific, fairly made with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, and cross-referenced to the warranty qualified. Specific disclosures in paras 2–10 can stand as specific disclosures (and note that most of them are actually helpful to us — see section 14 below).

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) – MAJOR DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Playbook:** delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Reasoning:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar extending to advisers and to anything "discoverable" — in effect a second whole-data-room disclosure plus a prudent-search standard, achieved through the knowledge clause instead of the disclosure clause. Together with Schedule 7 it would mean the warranties protect us only against matters not in the data room and not discoverable from it, which is very little.
- **Action:** Delete cl 8.3. If the Seller insists on a knowledge concept, it should be a seller-side knowledge qualifier on specified warranties only, by reference to named individuals after due enquiry, and expressly inapplicable to Title, capacity, fraud and the specific indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3) – MAJOR DEPARTURE, and Update contradicts Disclosure Letter
- **Seller Update:** "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."
- **Disclosure Letter para 2:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%); consent clause 11.2 has conditions at 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence conditions are satisfied** as at the letter date.
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Reasoning:** The Update says the matter is "addressed"; the Seller's own disclosure says it is not. A bare written consent subject to unsatisfied 11.3 conditions is not an effective consent — if the conditions fail post-Completion we may lose ~30% of revenue with no condition precedent protection. "Reasonable endeavours" also leaves the Seller free to abandon the effort if it becomes inconvenient.
- **Action:** Condition precedent requiring (i) Bluefen's unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 (or consent plus evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that all cl 11.3 conditions have been satisfied) and (ii) no notice of termination or adverse variation. Seller to use all reasonable endeavours (or best endeavours) and keep the Buyer informed. Consider a price-adjustment or walk right if consent is conditional. Request the current state of Bluefen correspondence immediately.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) – MAJOR DEPARTURE, Update contradicts Disclosure Letter
- **Seller Update:** ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Disclosure Letter para 3:** not repaid; no final discharge of security; change-control at 8.1 and discharge at 9.2.
- **Playbook:** current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; a post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval (not given).
- **Reasoning:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. If the facility is not repaid and discharged at Completion we are buying a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and a change-of-control trigger (cl 8.1) that Riverlark could call on the day we complete. A post-Completion release leaves us exposed to the Seller's performance and Riverlark's cooperation with no leverage.
- **Action:** Completion deliverables to include a payout letter current to the Completion date; funds flow to direct the payout amount from the purchase price to Riverlark; executed releases/discharges (and PPSR discharge) delivered at or conditional on Completion; Riverlark's written waiver or consent under cl 8.1. Do not entertain the post-Completion structure unless Amelia Frost approves and Riverlark provides an irrevocable undertaking.

### 10. Employee bonuses / funds flow (DD-005) – DEPARTURE
- **Seller Update:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Disclosure Letter para 5:** bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not in the funds flow**; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Reasoning:** The bonuses crystallise on Completion and are a liability of the Company (the employer), not the Seller, unless the documents say otherwise. "A matter for the Seller" is a statement of intent with no mechanism. If nothing is in the funds flow and nothing is in the price adjustment, the Company (i.e. us) pays AUD 420,000 plus on-costs post-Completion.
- **Action:** Either (a) a funds-flow line item deducting the bonuses plus employer superannuation, payroll tax and any other on-costs from the price, paid by the Company at Completion and reimbursed from the deduction; or (b) treatment as Debt/transaction expenses in the completion accounts; plus a specific indemnity for any shortfall. Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in writing. Do not quantify on-costs ourselves until DD confirms — flag as "AUD 420,000 plus on-costs (to be quantified)."

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) – DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate."
- **Disclosure Letter para 4:** DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but that is not independent verification of non-payment; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Reasoning:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000; it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials because the condition to transfer has not been met. An indemnity confined to "the payment" does not cover loss arising from defective IP ownership, third-party claims, inability to license the materials, or remediation. The cure (pay the fee, obtain confirmatory assignment) is cheap and should be done pre-Completion.
- **Action:** Broaden cl 11.1 to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any defect in title to, the Project Materials under any Ironquay SOW, including costs of obtaining assignment. Keep the SOW3 cure route: Seller to procure payment of outstanding SOW3 fees (whatever amount is verified) and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable. Neither party should treat AUD 180,000 as established; request bank evidence of payment status.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6; DD-006) – PARTIAL DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
- **Disclosure Letter para 6:** download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed, exact scope unknown, notification requirement undetermined; investigation preliminary; no confirmed breach; no loss amount.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is a conclusion the Disclosure Letter itself says cannot yet be drawn. We should not over-react (no established breach or harm) but equally should not accept a characterisation that may later be relied on as a disclosure against the privacy/data warranties.
- **Action:** Pre-Completion covenant: preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation, provide written updates and the final report, and notify the Buyer before any regulator or data-subject notification. Specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (uncapped by the general regime, or separately capped — to be negotiated), and a warranty that the Disclosure Letter is a complete and accurate description of the incident as at Completion. Do not state a number and do not accept the "operational matter" label.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – TO ASSESS, NO DEPARTURE YET
- **Seller:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Disclosure Letter para 8:** three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; read together; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's characterisation is unsupported by its own disclosure. But our playbook also does not treat these as Debt by default. The relevant questions are whether any amount is accrued at Completion (which should flow through working capital/debt), whether the renewals are committed or terminable, and whether the timing is being managed around Completion.
- **Action:** Request the renewal documents, term dates, termination rights and accrual status. Reserve position in the mark-up: treat as ordinary course only if confirmed; any accrued/unpaid amount at Completion into the completion accounts.

### 14. Tax / IP warranties – DEPARTURE
- **Seller:** "settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution; keep categories separate.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller is trying to close open items by assertion and by the cl 13 override sentence. We have not agreed Tax or IP terms. Note we are not seeking unlimited liability either — the point is that they are separate categories still under negotiation.
- **Action:** State expressly that Tax and IP warranties/indemnity, their cap and claims period remain open and are not governed by cl 12.1–12.3 absent express agreement.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012) – DEPARTURE, Update contradicts Disclosure Letter
- **Seller Update:** title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
- **Disclosure Letter para 10:** DD-012 "identifies the source relied on" and "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification."
- **Playbook:** independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's own letter concedes the register is merely its source. A company-maintained register is prima facie but not conclusive evidence and says nothing about encumbrances (e.g. any Riverlark security over the shares), authority of the Seller to sell, or third-party rights.
- **Action:** Buyer to run independent ASIC and PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller, obtain share certificates, Seller board/shareholder approvals, and Fundamental warranties on title, capacity and no encumbrances; Completion deliverables to include executed transfers, certificates and register updates. Completion conditional on clean searches.

---

## Cross-cutting observations

1. **Seller Update vs Disclosure Letter inconsistencies.** On Bluefen, Riverlark and Title, the Update asserts matters are "addressed"/"evidenced" while the Disclosure Letter says they are not. Point this out in our cover note — it undermines the "fair and balanced" framing and gives us the moral high ground on process.
2. **Layered protection for the Seller.** The package stacks (a) whole-data-room disclosure, (b) a constructive-knowledge bar extending to advisers and "discoverable" matters, (c) limitations applying to "all Claims," and (d) a default rule that every limitation applies across categories. Each on its own is objectionable; together they would leave the warranties with almost no practical content. Our response should address them as a system, not one by one.
3. **Para 1.4 reservation.** Acceptable as a non-admission clause, but it must not be read as qualifying the Seller's obligation to make specific disclosures or as neutralising the facts actually disclosed in paras 2–10. Our mark-up should confirm the Disclosure Letter does not operate to limit the specific indemnities.
4. **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The Disclosure Letter characterises these as notification-only / no consent required. Not a playbook item, but we should verify the clauses ourselves rather than accept the characterisation, and add the lease notification as a Completion or post-Completion deliverable.
5. **Authority discipline.** Two Seller positions coincide with our fallbacks (20% cap; 18 months). We must not accept either, or hint that they are acceptable, without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft. Any such concession should be sought, if at all, only as part of a package in which the Seller moves on Riverlark, Bluefen, Fundamental/Title and fraud.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Our mark-up position | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 25% / AUD 6,000,000 | High |
| 2 | Thresholds | De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar | High |
| 3 | Claims period / override | 24 months; delete "applies to all Claims" default | High |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Separate regime: 100%, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge | Non-negotiable |
| 5 | Fraud carve-out | Carve out fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct from all caps, time limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance | Non-negotiable |
| 6 | Disclosure | Specific fair disclosure only; delete paras 1.1–1.2 as general disclosure | High |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Delete cl 8.3; seller named-persons qualifier only, never for title/capacity/fraud/indemnities | High |
| 8 | Bluefen | CP: effective consent + evidence cl 11.3 conditions satisfied pre-Completion; not consent-on-delivery; endeavours standard strengthened | Critical (~30% revenue) |
| 9 | Riverlark | Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion; cl 8.1 waiver; no post-Completion release without Frost approval + irrevocable undertaking | Critical (AUD 3.2m) |
| 10 | Bonuses | AUD 420,000 + on-costs as funds-flow line item or seller-funded; specific indemnity | High |
| 11 | Ironquay | Broaden indemnity to IP ownership/title; preserve SOW3 cure; confirmatory assignment as deliverable; verify AUD 180,000 | High |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | Preserve logs, investigate, update covenant; specific indemnity; no characterisation either way | Medium–High |
| 13 | Sandbar | Request documents; no automatic Debt treatment; accrued amounts into completion accounts | Medium |
| 14 | Tax / IP | Expressly open; separate categories; not under general regime | High |
| 15 | Title | Independent ASIC/PPSR searches, certificates, authority evidence; DD-012 not sufficient | High |

**Immediate next steps:**
1. Issue mark-up on the above; cover note to highlight the Update/Disclosure Letter inconsistencies.
2. Information requests to Seller: Bluefen correspondence and cl 11.3 status; Riverlark payout and security schedule; Ironquay payment evidence; bonus on-cost position; DD-006 investigation status; Sandbar renewal terms.
3. Commission independent title/encumbrance searches now.
4. Brief Amelia Frost on the two fallback points so she can decide, in advance, whether and when any authority will be given — but no authority to be assumed in the meantime.
=== END ADVICE ===
